transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I decided to come in today because I've been feeling really uneasy lately. I am convinced that I am being watched and monitored by certain people, or maybe some kind of organization. It has just gotten to be too much to handle on my own.
Have you also heard any voices or seen things that other people don't seem to hear or see?

Yes, I have. I've been hearing whispering voices when no one else is around, and sometimes I see shadowy figures moving in the corners of the room. It is really unsettling because I know other people can't see or hear them.
How has your mood been lately? Have you been feeling very down and depressed, or perhaps unusually energized and hyperactive?

I wouldn't say I've felt particularly depressed or unusually energized. Instead, I just feel really flat, empty, and indifferent to everything around me. It's like my emotions are just dialed way down.
Have you ever had periods in your life where you felt severely depressed, or on the contrary, extremely energized and active for days or weeks?
No, I've never had periods of severe depression or extreme high energy. My mood doesn't really fluctuate like that.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of being watched, hearing the whispering voices, and seeing the shadowy figures?
It's been going on for about eight months now. It started around then and just hasn't stopped, and honestly, it's making me feel so exhausted and anxious all the time.

latest_inference.note: The patient has experienced persecutory beliefs, auditory hallucinations (whispering voices), visual hallucinations (shadowy figures), and negative symptoms (flat affect, feeling empty/indifferent) for about eight months. They explicitly deny history of major depressive episodes or manic/hypomanic episodes, which rules out Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Disorder with Psychotic Features, and Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features. Delusional Disorder is ruled out due to prominent auditory and visual hallucinations. The duration of symptoms is greater than six months, which meets the duration criteria for Schizophrenia. I have gathered sufficient evidence to confirm Schizophrenia as the primary diagnosis.
